title: Chapter9
description: Finnish vocabulary: celebrations, baking, invitations and verbs

questions.question: Ingredient
questions.explanation: 'Aines' means ingredient; its genitive is 'aineksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I need all the ingredients for the cake.

questions.question: To suggest
questions.explanation: 'Ehdottaa' (type 1 verb) means to suggest; 'ehdotan' is 'I suggest'.
questions.exampletranslate: I suggest that we celebrate on Saturday.

questions.question: Absolutely
questions.explanation: 'Ehdottomasti' means absolutely.
questions.exampletranslate: I will absolutely come to the party.

questions.question: Life
questions.explanation: 'Elämä' means life.
questions.exampletranslate: Life is beautiful.

questions.question: Before
questions.explanation: 'Ennen' means before.
questions.exampletranslate: I'll come before the party.

questions.question: Special / Peculiar
questions.explanation: 'Erikoinen' means special or peculiar; its genitive is 'erikoisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: This is a special day.

questions.question: Funeral
questions.explanation: 'Hautajaiset' means funeral (a plural word); its genitive is 'hautajaisten'.
questions.exampletranslate: I attend the funeral.

questions.question: Moment
questions.explanation: 'Hetki' means moment; its genitive is 'hetken'.
questions.exampletranslate: Wait a moment, please.

questions.question: Yeast
questions.explanation: 'Hiiva' means yeast.
questions.exampletranslate: Yeast is needed for the sweet bun.

questions.question: Jam
questions.explanation: 'Hillo' means jam.
questions.exampletranslate: I put jam on the pancake.

questions.question: To notice
questions.explanation: 'Huomata' (type 4 verb) means to notice; 'huomaan' is 'I notice'.
questions.exampletranslate: I notice that you are happy.

questions.question: To shout
questions.explanation: 'Huutaa' (type 1 verb) means to shout; 'huudan' is 'I shout'.
questions.exampletranslate: Don't shout so loudly.

questions.question: Wedding
questions.explanation: 'Häät' means wedding (a plural word); its genitive is 'häiden'.
questions.exampletranslate: We go to the wedding on Saturday.

questions.question: Lovely
questions.explanation: 'Ihana' means lovely or wonderful.
questions.exampletranslate: This is a lovely surprise.

questions.question: To wonder / marvel
questions.explanation: 'Ihmetellä' (type 3 verb) means to wonder or marvel; 'ihmettelen' is 'I wonder'.
questions.exampletranslate: I wonder why he didn't come.

questions.question: Registration / Enrolment
questions.explanation: 'Ilmoittautuminen' means registration or enrolment; its genitive is 'ilmoittautumisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: Registration for the event is open.

questions.question: To hate / detest
questions.explanation: 'Inhota' (type 4 verb) means to hate or detest; 'inhoan' is 'I hate' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I hate being late.

questions.question: Somewhere
questions.explanation: 'Jossain' means somewhere.
questions.exampletranslate: The party is somewhere in the centre.

questions.question: Drink / Beverage
questions.explanation: 'Juoma' means drink or beverage.
questions.exampletranslate: I offer a drink to the guests.

questions.question: To run
questions.explanation: 'Juosta' (type 2 verb) means to run; 'juoksen' is 'I run'.
questions.exampletranslate: I run every morning.

questions.question: After
questions.explanation: 'Jälkeen' means after (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: After the party we clean up.

questions.question: Dessert
questions.explanation: 'Jälkiruoka' means dessert; its genitive is 'jälkiruoan'.
questions.exampletranslate: For dessert there is cake.

questions.question: All / Everything
questions.explanation: 'Kaikki' means all or everything.
questions.exampletranslate: All the guests are here.

questions.question: Sauce
questions.explanation: 'Kastike' means sauce; its genitive is 'kastikkeen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I make a sauce for the meatballs.

questions.question: To tell
questions.explanation: 'Kertoa' (type 1 verb) means to tell; 'kerron' is 'I tell'.
questions.exampletranslate: I tell a funny story.

questions.question: Letter
questions.explanation: 'Kirje' means letter; its genitive is 'kirjeen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I send the invitation in a letter.

questions.question: However / Still
questions.explanation: 'Kuitenkin' means however or still.
questions.exampletranslate: I was tired, but I came anyway.

questions.question: Anyone / No one
questions.explanation: 'Kukaan' means anyone (in negative sentences, no one).
questions.exampletranslate: No one knew about the surprise.

questions.question: To die
questions.explanation: 'Kuolla' (type 3 verb) means to die; 'kuolen' is 'I die'.
questions.exampletranslate: The plant died in winter.

questions.question: Invitation
questions.explanation: 'Kutsu' means invitation.
questions.exampletranslate: I got an invitation to the birthday party.

questions.question: To download / load
questions.explanation: 'Ladata' (type 4 verb) means to download, load or charge; 'lataan' is 'I download/load'.
questions.exampletranslate: I download the invitation to my phone.

questions.question: Gift
questions.explanation: 'Lahja' means gift.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a gift for a friend.

questions.question: Gift card
questions.explanation: 'Lahjakortti' means gift card; its genitive is 'lahjakortin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I give a gift card as a present.

questions.question: Meatballs
questions.explanation: 'Lihapullat' means meatballs (a plural word); its genitive is 'lihapullien'.
questions.exampletranslate: I make meatballs for the party.

questions.question: To promise
questions.explanation: 'Luvata' (type 4 verb) means to promise; 'lupaan' is 'I promise'.
questions.exampletranslate: I promise to come on time.

questions.question: Travel gift card
questions.explanation: 'Matkalahjakortti' means a travel gift card; its genitive is 'matkalahjakortin'.
questions.exampletranslate: We got a travel gift card as a wedding present.

questions.question: By (a deadline)
questions.explanation: 'Mennessä' means by (a certain deadline), used with the genitive.
questions.exampletranslate: Register by Friday.

questions.question: Gladly
questions.explanation: 'Mielellään' means gladly.
questions.exampletranslate: I gladly come to the party.

questions.question: To think / ponder
questions.explanation: 'Miettiä' (type 1 verb) means to think or ponder; 'mietin' is 'I think' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I think about what to buy as a gift.

questions.question: Until / Up to
questions.explanation: 'Saakka' means until or up to, as in 'mihin saakka' (up to what point).
questions.exampletranslate: The party lasts until morning.

questions.question: To reminisce
questions.explanation: 'Muistella' (type 3 verb) means to reminisce; 'muistelen' is 'I reminisce' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: We reminisce about old times.

questions.question: To move (change residence)
questions.explanation: 'Muuttaa' (type 1 verb) means to move (e.g. change residence) or to change; 'muutan' is 'I move'.
questions.exampletranslate: I move to a new apartment.

questions.question: Naming ceremony / party
questions.explanation: 'Nimiäiset' means a naming ceremony or party (a plural word); its genitive is 'nimiäisten'.
questions.exampletranslate: A naming party is held for the baby.

questions.question: To own
questions.explanation: 'Omistaa' (type 1 verb) means to own; 'omistan' is 'I own'.
questions.exampletranslate: I own my own house.

questions.question: To succeed
questions.explanation: 'Onnistua' (type 1 verb) means to succeed; 'onnistun' is 'I succeed'.
questions.exampletranslate: The surprise succeeded well.

questions.question: To congratulate
questions.explanation: 'Onnitella' (type 3 verb) means to congratulate; 'onnittelen' is 'I congratulate' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I congratulate you on your birthday.

questions.question: To participate
questions.explanation: 'Osallistua' (type 1 verb) means to participate; 'osallistun' is 'I participate' (used with 'mihin').
questions.exampletranslate: I participate in the party.

questions.question: To know how to / be able to
questions.explanation: 'Osata' (type 4 verb) means to know how to or be able to; 'osaan' is 'I know how to'.
questions.exampletranslate: I know how to make sweet buns.

questions.question: Pancake (oven pancake)
questions.explanation: 'Pannukakku' means pancake (often a Finnish oven pancake); its genitive is 'pannukakun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I bake a pancake in the oven.

questions.question: Bean
questions.explanation: 'Papu' means bean; its genitive is 'pavun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I add beans to the soup.

questions.question: Pie / Pastry
questions.explanation: 'Piirakka' means pie or pastry; its genitive is 'piirakan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I bake a berry pie.

questions.question: To give a speech
questions.explanation: 'Pitää puheen' means to give a speech; 'pidän puheen' is 'I give a speech'.
questions.exampletranslate: The father gives a speech at the wedding.

questions.question: Sweet bun (pulla)
questions.explanation: 'Pulla' means a sweet bun (a Finnish cardamom bun).
questions.exampletranslate: I serve coffee and sweet buns.

questions.question: Nut
questions.explanation: 'Pähkinä' means nut.
questions.exampletranslate: There are nuts in the cake.

questions.question: To argue / quarrel
questions.explanation: 'Riidellä' (type 3 verb) means to argue or quarrel; 'riitelen' is 'I argue'.
questions.exampletranslate: They argue often.

questions.question: Christening / Baptism party
questions.explanation: 'Ristiäiset' means a christening or baptism party (a plural word); its genitive is 'ristiäisten'.
questions.exampletranslate: The baby is baptized at the christening.

questions.question: Trash / Litter
questions.explanation: 'Roska' means trash or litter.
questions.exampletranslate: I take the trash out after the party.

questions.question: Mushroom
questions.explanation: 'Sieni' means mushroom; its genitive is 'sienen'.
questions.exampletranslate: We gather mushrooms from the forest.

questions.question: So / Therefore
questions.explanation: 'Siis' means so, therefore or thus.
questions.exampletranslate: So you are coming to the party?

questions.question: To ring / sound
questions.explanation: 'Soida' (type 2 verb) means to ring or sound; 'se soi' means 'it rings'.
questions.exampletranslate: The phone rings at the party.

questions.question: Agreed / Arranged
questions.explanation: 'Sovittu' means agreed or arranged; its genitive is 'sovitun'.
questions.exampletranslate: The time is already agreed.

questions.question: To kiss
questions.explanation: 'Suudella' (type 3 verb) means to kiss; 'suutelen' is 'I kiss' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: He kisses the bride.

questions.question: To plan
questions.explanation: 'Suunnitella' (type 3 verb) means to plan; 'suunnittelen' is 'I plan' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I plan the party.

questions.question: Birthday (party)
questions.explanation: 'Syntymäpäivät' means a birthday party (a plural word); its genitive is 'syntymäpäivien'.
questions.exampletranslate: We celebrate the birthday on Saturday.

questions.question: To feel like (doing)
questions.explanation: 'Tehdä mieli' means to feel like; 'minun tekee mieli' means 'I feel like'.
questions.exampletranslate: I feel like having cake.

questions.question: Event / Occasion
questions.explanation: 'Tilaisuus' means event or occasion; its genitive is 'tilaisuuden'.
questions.exampletranslate: This is a festive occasion.

questions.question: To order
questions.explanation: 'Tilata' (type 4 verb) means to order; 'tilaan' is 'I order'.
questions.exampletranslate: I order a cake for the party.

questions.question: To come along
questions.explanation: 'Tulla mukaan' means to come along; 'tulen mukaan' is 'I come along'.
questions.exampletranslate: Will you come along to the party?

questions.question: To know (a person) / feel
questions.explanation: 'Tuntea' (type 1 verb) means to know (a person) or to feel; 'tunnen' is 'I know/feel'.
questions.exampletranslate: I know all the guests.

questions.question: To bring
questions.explanation: 'Tuoda' (type 2 verb) means to bring; 'tuon' is 'I bring'.
questions.exampletranslate: I bring a gift to the party.

questions.question: Housewarming party
questions.explanation: 'Tupaantuliaiset' means a housewarming party (a plural word); its genitive is 'tupaantuliaisten'.
questions.exampletranslate: We hold a housewarming party in the new home.

questions.question: To fill / turn (a certain age)
questions.explanation: 'Täyttää' (type 1 verb) means to fill or to turn a certain age; 'täytän' is 'I fill / I turn'.
questions.exampletranslate: I turn 30 tomorrow.

questions.question: By accident / accidentally
questions.explanation: 'Vahingossa' means by accident or accidentally.
questions.exampletranslate: I broke the glass by accident.

questions.question: To lie
questions.explanation: 'Valehdella' (type 3 verb) means to lie; 'valehtelen' is 'I lie'.
questions.exampletranslate: Don't lie to me.

questions.question: Wheat flour
questions.explanation: 'Vehnäjauhot' means wheat flour (a plural word); its genitive is 'vehnäjauhojen'.
questions.exampletranslate: Wheat flour is needed for the sweet bun.

questions.question: Guest
questions.explanation: 'Vieras' means guest (also stranger or foreign); its genitive is 'vieraan'.
questions.exampletranslate: The guests arrive at six o'clock.

questions.question: Grape
questions.explanation: 'Viinirypäle' means grape; its genitive is 'viinirypäleen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I serve grapes.

questions.question: Contact information
questions.explanation: 'Yhteystiedot' means contact information (a plural word); its genitive is 'yhteystietojen'.
questions.exampletranslate: Give me your contact information.

questions.question: Private event
questions.explanation: 'Yksityistilaisuus' means a private event; its genitive is 'yksityistilaisuuden'.
questions.exampletranslate: The restaurant has a private event today.

questions.question: Surprise
questions.explanation: 'Yllätys' means surprise; its genitive is 'yllätyksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: This is a fun surprise!

questions.question: Oil
questions.explanation: 'Öljy' means oil.
questions.exampletranslate: I fry in oil.
